The researchers working on SpudCell hope that it will eventually be a platform for biotechnology that will allow a simple cell to be engineered in scores of useful ways. SpudCell could potentially be misused, so its researchers are taking security seriously from the start - its DNA and proteins are engineered so that it can only survive on an exotic diet of chemicals not found in nature.

articles.headline: GhostMap: The Android flaw that crashes your phone before you open the app
articles.blurb: An APK entry using a nonstandard compression method slips past libziparchive's size check, while libandroidfw memory-maps it at its full declared size. As a result, any process that reads a malformed resource receives a SIGBUS. That flaw lets an app with no code or permissions trap system_server in a boot loop that only a factory reset clears, or cause its own icon to crash on every uninstall screen. Bitdefender found it when a packed banking dropper in the wild crashed its emulators, but the persistent boot loop was its own escalation. Google declined to ship a security fix even though the bug reproduces on Android 10 through 17. With no patch coming, defenders should flag APKs whose ZIP entries use compression methods other than stored or deflate before they're installed, since an on-device warning may come too late.

articles.headline: Escaping Firecracker from Guest Userspace
articles.blurb: Coinspect demonstrated a Firecracker sandbox escape from guest userspace. CVE-2026-122192 allowed a guest to read and modify live Firecracker VMM memory and gain code execution in the host-side process. The flaw stemmed from a failed memory replacement after a snapshot-backed RAM discard, leaving a stale KVM memory slot pointing to reused VMM memory. A second issue, FC-03, allowed VMM code to use io_uring to perform host operations blocked by seccomp, including sending a network message to a host listener. Firecracker v0.23.0 through v1.16.1 are affected. v1.16.2 and v1.17.0 fix the escape.

articles.headline: The SOC Files 5: Ghost in the pipeline, or a fileless SharePoint breach by Storm-2603
articles.blurb: Storm-2603 used the ONYPHE scanner to check a SharePoint server for ToolShell (CVE-2025-53770), waited three days, and on Christmas Eve loaded a webshell directly into IIS's w3wp.exe process memory. The webshell activated only for a specific User-Agent, tunneled into the internal network with suo5, escalated to SYSTEM using EfsPotato, and then moved to a vulnerable Velociraptor build, an EDR-killer driver, and a blocked Warlock ransomware attempt. Kaspersky attributed the intrusion with moderate confidence. Defenders should hunt for IIS paths that resolve in config but have no file on disk, which appear as IIS-Configuration ETW events 25 and 47 without the usual file-change monitoring events. Kaspersky has released CLRDeserializationExploitFinder to flag the deserialization exploit itself.

articles.headline: synology-nas-cli (GitHub Repo)

It shows each fix as a before-and-after dry-run plan, applies it, and reads every setting back to confirm. If encryption is already running, it can freeze the encryptor with SIGSTOP and capture its memory to recover keys. It's a zero-dependency Python CLI with an MCP server, so a Claude Code or Codex agent can run the audit end to end.

articles.headline: Sectiv (GitHub Repo)

Testers can load two accounts to help the model reason about broken access control. It masks cookies, tokens, and JWTs before sending traffic to providers like OpenAI, Claude, DeepSeek, or a local Ollama model. Skills can be imported, exported, and tailored per target, and findings export to HTML, Markdown, or JSON for reporting.

Publicly shared items lose end-to-end encryption, even with Advanced Data Protection enabled. Apple can remove files, block accounts, prevent re-registration, and contact law enforcement. It has not defined “harmful,” explained the screening method, said whether people review flags, or confirmed whether existing public links are covered.

The run produced 291 information-leak proofs of concept, patches for identified flaws, and at least 10 novel exploitation techniques. It cost $1.21 million in API credits, or $1,279 per exploit. OpenAI says unpatched systems with low-privileged access should be treated as accessible to well-resourced attackers with root access.

articles.headline: Low pressure in US midwest brings unseasonable heat to New York and Boston
articles.blurb: Further south this week, severe thunderstorms affected midterms voting in Florida, Oklahoma and Colorado Despite the rapid descent into autumn in the northern hemisphere, parts of eastern North America have experienced an exceptionally late taste of summer in recent days. Temperatures approached 23C (73F) in New York and Boston, about 7-10C above what is expected in early November. The unseasonable warmth spilled into parts of eastern Canada, with temperatures exceeding 20C, about 10-15C above normal for the time of year. The balmy conditions were caused by an area of low pressure in the US midwest, dragging up exceptionally warm air from the Gulf of Mexico along its eastern flank. This area of low pressure will gradually drift eastwards, allowing temperatures to fall closer to the average. Further south, severe thunderstorms have resulted in numerous flood warnings and evacuation warnings being issued this week across many states, with disruptive weather affecting polling stations in Florida, Oklahoma and Colorado. The powerful thunderstorms even resulted in a tornado touching down in Keyes, Oklahoma, forcing the relocation of a polling station. The tornado caused extensive damage, although no causalities have been reported. Officials across many states have requested federal funding assistance after the extreme weather resulted in widespread damage to homes and infrastructure.
